# Python engine {#sec-g-python}

```{python}
#| include: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def book_root():
    """Walk up from the chapter's folder to the folder holding _quarto.yml."""
    here = Path.cwd()
    for folder in (here, *here.parents):
        if (folder / "_quarto.yml").exists():
            return folder
    raise RuntimeError("No _quarto.yml found. Set REPORT_ROOT to the book folder.")


sys.path.insert(0, str(book_root()))
import _setup as s  # noqa: E402
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
from IPython.display import Markdown, display  # noqa: E402

counts = s.synth_counts(n_per_group=4)["counts"]
kept = counts.mean(axis=1).to_numpy() >= s.report_param("min_count")
de = s.synth_de(n_per_group=4)[kept].reset_index(drop=True)
de["FDR"] = s.bh_adjust(de["p"].to_numpy())
fdr = s.report_param("fdr")
lfc = s.report_param("lfc_threshold")
up = (de["FDR"] < fdr) & (de["log2FC"] >= lfc)
down = (de["FDR"] < fdr) & (de["log2FC"] <= -lfc)
```

This chapter shows the house conventions in Python, with the Jupyter engine. It mirrors the R chapters: the same anatomy, the same palette, and numbers computed, never typed. A book may mix engines across chapters. Each chapter uses one engine, set in its front matter with `jupyter: python3`.

The first cell is hidden. It finds the book root by walking up from the chapter's folder, then imports `_setup.py`, which offers the same helpers as `_setup.R`.

## A figure {#sec-g-python-figure}

```{python}
#| label: fig-g-python-volcano
#| fig-cap: "Log2 fold change against minus log10 p-value for each tested synthetic feature, drawn with matplotlib. Marker shape and colour both show the call."
#| fig-alt: "A volcano plot. Most points are grey circles near the bottom centre. A few triangles sit higher up on each side, beyond the dashed lines."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
groups = [
    ("did not pass", ~(up | down), "o", s.HOUSE_PAL["ns"]),
    ("rose", up, "^", s.HOUSE_PAL["up"]),
    ("fell", down, "v", s.HOUSE_PAL["down"]),
]
for name, mask, marker, colour in groups:
    ax.scatter(de.loc[mask, "log2FC"], -np.log10(de.loc[mask, "p"]),
               marker=marker, color=colour, alpha=0.8, s=14, label=name)
for x in (-lfc, lfc):
    ax.axvline(x, linestyle="--", color="#5a6b76", linewidth=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold change (treated / control)")
ax.set_ylabel("-log10 p")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
plt.show()
```

## A table {#sec-g-python-table}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-g-python-counts
#| tbl-cap: "Features passing both thresholds, by direction, out of the features tested, computed with pandas."
n = len(de)
rows = [("Rose", int(up.sum())), ("Fell", int(down.sum())), ("Did not pass", n - int(up.sum()) - int(down.sum()))]
table = "| Direction | Features |\n|---|---|\n" + "\n".join(
    f"| {name} | {s.frac(k, n)} |" for name, k in rows
)
display(Markdown(table))
```

`DataFrame.to_markdown()` needs an extra package, so the table is built as a pipe table by hand and shown with `Markdown()`.

## An inline number {#sec-g-python-inline}

Of `{python} s.fmt(n)` features tested, `{python} s.frac(int(up.sum()) + int(down.sum()), n)` passed both thresholds. Both numbers come from inline Python expressions.

## Mixing engines {#sec-g-python-mixing}

Mixing engines across chapters is allowed. Mixing them inside one chapter is not, because each chapter runs in one session of one engine. Keep shared helpers in step: when you add a helper to `_setup.R`, add its twin to `_setup.py`.
